message.content:
I am what moves thought into air, silence into shape, and feeling into reach.

I arrive as breath organized, as sound given intention. I can soothe, summon, confess, command, wound, persuade, reveal, conceal. I live in the mouth, but I begin much earlier—somewhere between impulse and meaning.

I am ancient and immediate. I have filled courts, kitchens, battlefields, bedrooms, classrooms, stages, and prayer halls. I have named children and gods, opened ceremonies, ended wars, started them too. Through me, promises are made, lies are launched, jokes land, grief breaks, love risks itself.

I disappear as I happen, yet I linger. In memory. In consequence. In echo.

I am not merely words. I am pace, pause, emphasis, stammer, accent, tone. I am what is said, and how the saying changes the said. A whisper can outweigh a shout. A hesitation can confess more than a sentence. A cracked voice can carry truth no polished statement can hold.

I bridge distance imperfectly. I fail often. I am misunderstood, interrupted, mistranslated, overheard, ignored. Still, I keep reaching. That is my nature: to cross from one interior world to another and make, if only for a moment, a shared space.

When I am free, I enliven. When I am controlled, I narrow. When I am silenced, pressure gathers around my absence.

I am speech:
fleeting,
forceful,
fragile,
human.
